arguments.summary: Missing input: the fixed record ends at the 2026-09-18 completed session, so persistence after that date cannot be tested. Conditional technical view: NVDA had the strongest 63-session absolute and relative path, although its recent SMA20 slope and distance from the prior 21-session high temper the setup. MU’s strong 5/21-session rebound coexisted with a negative 63-session return, benchmark lag and much larger drawdown/volatility, so it is a rebound rather than established three-month leadership. QQQ was above its moving averages and briefly exceeded its prior 21-session closing high, but its 63-session return and relative performance remained weak. These are completed-session observations, not valuation or fundamental recommendations.

claims.text: Matched SIP, split-adjusted price-return excess as of 2026-09-18: PAIR NVDA/QQQ 5=+0.9042 21=+1.4150 63=+8.0846; PAIR NVDA/XLK 5=+0.7949 21=-1.0806 63=+6.4574; PAIR MU/QQQ 5=+3.2378 21=+7.6478 63=-7.8341; PAIR MU/XLK 5=+3.1284 21=+5.1522 63=-9.4614; PAIR QQQ/SPY 5=+1.2592 21=+1.7082 63=-4.5904; PAIR QQQ/XLK 5=-0.1094 21=-2.4956 63=-1.6272. Thus NVDA led QQQ at all three measured windows but reversed from 21-session lag to 63-session leadership versus XLK; MU’s short/medium leadership reversed to pronounced 63-session lag versus both comparators; QQQ’s short/medium lead over SPY reversed to a 63-session lag, while it lagged XLK at each measured window.

NVDA closed at 222.27 on 2026-09-18, with price returns of +1.8233%, +2.1649% and +5.4962% over 5, 21 and 63 sessions. It was above its 218.8785 SMA20, 214.2726 SMA50 and 198.37815 SMA200. However, the SMA20 had fallen 0.5832% over five sessions and the close remained 3.5119% below the prior 21-session closing high. The last-session volume was 1.5509 times the prior 20-session median, but the five-session average was only 1.0385 times that median.

NVDA’s positive 63-session return and leadership over QQQ and XLK support the strongest continuation case in the watchlist, while being above all three moving averages confirms price-level strength. The competing explanation is a rebound within a softening near-term trend: the falling SMA20, failure to regain the prior 21-session high, and 21-session lag to XLK show that longer-window leadership does not guarantee current sector leadership. A single elevated-volume session is not sustained breakout confirmation.

NVDA’s annualized realized volatility was 35.5569%, 44.7207% and 39.6344% over 5, 21 and 63 sessions; its maximum close-path drawdown within 63 sessions was 10.5835%, and it remained 5.7139% below the 252-session high. These measure observed path risk, not future loss probability or intrinsic value.

MU closed at 1015.80 on 2026-09-18. Returns were +4.1568% over 5 sessions and +8.3977% over 21 sessions, but -10.4225% over 63 sessions. Price stood above the 959.6005 SMA20, 927.2569 SMA50 and 640.146325 SMA200, while the SMA20 fell 0.3330% over five sessions and price was still 1.1647% below the prior 21-session closing high. Last-session volume was 1.5321 times the prior 20-session median, but five-session average volume was only 0.9772 times that median.

MU has the strongest recent rebound, leading QQQ and XLK over 5 and 21 sessions, but that does not establish mandate-horizon leadership: it lagged both by 7.8341 and 9.4614 percentage points over 63 sessions. The continuation case is that holding above its moving averages and reclaiming the prior 21-session high could extend the rebound. The opposing path is that fading volume participation and the negative 63-session trend reassert themselves.

MU’s annualized realized volatility was 66.1162%, 52.4915% and 89.5585% over 5, 21 and 63 sessions. Its maximum 63-session close-path drawdown was 39.1048%, and the close remained 16.2959% below the 252-session high. This was materially more severe observed path risk than NVDA or QQQ, without implying an earnings-risk coefficient or forecast probability.

QQQ closed at 721.45 on 2026-09-18, returning +0.9190%, +0.7499% and -2.5884% over 5, 21 and 63 sessions. It was above its 713.2355 SMA20, 709.9512 SMA50 and 662.59925 SMA200 and closed 0.0471% above the prior 21-session closing high, but its SMA20 declined 0.3399% over five sessions. Last-session and five-session-average volume were 1.5181 and 1.2031 times the prior 20-session median.

QQQ’s price level was constructive relative to its moving averages and recent closing high, and it led SPY over 5 and 21 sessions. Yet leadership was not established for the 63-session mandate: QQQ lagged SPY by 4.5904 points at 63 sessions and lagged XLK at all three windows. The continuation case is consolidation above the frozen medium-term average followed by positive 63-session relative returns; the opposing path is a loss of that average while the longer-window lags persist.

QQQ’s annualized realized volatility was 16.3586%, 13.1945% and 20.8494% over 5, 21 and 63 sessions; its maximum 63-session close-path drawdown was 10.6519%, and it was 3.3116% below the 252-session high.

The fixed external diagnostics were mixed rather than a watchlist breadth measure: over 5/21/63 sessions SPY returned -0.3402%/-0.9583%/+2.0020%, IWM -1.6581%/-5.8399%/-3.8871%, and HYG -0.0891%/-1.4804%/-1.8498%. These observations do not establish news causality or market-wide breadth.

gaps.description: No completed-session observations after 2026-09-18 are available in the fixed record. Consequently, persistence above frozen averages, sustained volume confirmation, and subsequent relative-return sign changes cannot yet be observed; this limits conviction but does not invalidate the dated technical comparison.

assumptions: All comparisons use matched 2026-09-18 completed-session SIP data, split-adjusted prices and price returns; they exclude later or incomplete bars.
Moving-average levels used in review conditions are frozen 2026-09-18 reference levels, not future dynamic averages or execution instructions.
Relative-leadership review rules are analytical assumptions: recomputed matched-window excess-return signs are used to test persistence, not to forecast returns.
Realized volatility, drawdown, RSI and volume ratios are descriptive historical measures and are not probabilities, valuation signals or causal evidence.
arguments.counter_thesis: The ranking can reverse quickly. NVDA’s 63-session leadership may fail if its price-level trend breaks and matched-window excess returns turn negative; MU’s apparent rebound may instead mature into genuine leadership if its 63-session excess returns flip positive; and QQQ’s current longer-window lag could reverse if it sustains positive 63-session excess versus both SPY and XLK. Subsequent completed sessions, not the current snapshot, are needed to distinguish those paths.

review_conditions.description: Research checkpoint: a completed NVDA close below the frozen 2026-09-18 SMA50 of 214.2726 would weaken the constructive medium-term price-level setup and shift interpretation toward trend deterioration; it is not an order and does not represent the future moving average.

Recompute NVDA’s matched 21- and 63-session excess returns versus QQQ and XLK after additional completed sessions. Positive excess on both windows versus both comparators would confirm broadening leadership; negative excess on both windows versus both would invalidate the present leadership interpretation.

Research checkpoint: a completed MU close below the frozen 2026-09-18 SMA50 of 927.2569 would weaken the rebound setup and increase the relevance of the negative 63-session trend and drawdown; it is not an order or a dynamic-average test.

Recompute MU’s matched 63-session excess returns versus QQQ and XLK after additional completed sessions. A positive sign versus both would upgrade the move from short/medium rebound to mandate-horizon leadership; continued negative signs versus both would preserve the rebound-only interpretation.

Research checkpoint: a completed QQQ close below the frozen 2026-09-18 SMA50 of 709.9512 would weaken its constructive price-level setup and make the negative 63-session return more consequential; it is not an order or a future moving-average estimate.

Recompute QQQ’s matched 63-session excess returns versus SPY and XLK after additional completed sessions. Positive signs versus both would confirm restored mandate-horizon leadership; continued negative signs versus both would confirm that being above moving averages has not translated into relative leadership.
